claims.kickoff_quote: Step 7's planner does not load PATTERNS.md on its own, so it has to be handed to it explicitly there.
claims.reasoning: pattern-mapper's <downstream_consumer> block asserts the handoff as if it were automatic, complete with a table of how planner uses each section (lines 67-73). I grepped planner.md (52 KB) for `PATTERNS.md`, `pattern-mapper`, and `analog`: zero hits for the first two, and the only `analog` hit is line 1215's unrelated stop-reading rule. Neither agent enforces the handoff, so the KICKOFF sentence is the ONLY thing that gets PATTERNS.md into the planner — it is load-bearing and must be KEPT, and the real defect is pattern-mapper's aspirational downstream-consumer table plus planner's missing input.

I grepped the whole file for `if exists|missing|absent|abort|halt|stop|refuse|empty`; the only other hits are lines 127 and 312, both about early-stopping the analog search, and <success_criteria> (lines 320-328) never requires the inputs to be non-empty. The KICKOFF warning is therefore compensating and must be KEPT; the fix belongs in the agent.
